target_customer: Parents buying summer camps and classes, and camp providers paying commission
problem: Parents found camps through scattered directories; providers lacked easy online registration.
business_model: Marketplace with 10 to 20 percent commission on sales through registration software
product_category: Kids camps marketplace, later kids coding classes

founders.name: Emmie Chang
previous_startups: Largest summer technology camp in Texas
Math ed-tech software used in over 35 school districts
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Education not found.

competitors.name: Sigby
competitors.what: Camp discovery service covered alongside Camperoo

technical_complexity.rationale: Listings marketplace with booking software for providers.

defensibility.rationale: Supply of about 1,500 activities from 250 providers helped, but directories and registration vendors were easy to copy.

market_need_then: TechCrunch March 2014 said Camperoo had about 1,500 activities from 250 providers and described existing services as directories rather than a marketplace.

rebrands.why: Company moved to teaching kids engineering and programming

brand_strength.rationale: Playful name suited a family camps marketplace, but no mascot or community evidence found and a rebrand followed the pivot.

pivots.to: FutureLeague, engineering and coding classes for ages 6 to 12 and corporate events

outcome_analysis: Camperoo launched a camps marketplace in Houston and Palo Alto, joined YC Winter 2014, then became FutureLeague teaching kids to code. The company is listed inactive and the founder now builds a different product. No post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public, and the pivot failure code is tentative.
notes: Funding conflict: CB Insights shows 20K from YC in Jan 2014 with a 300K total; Wefunder reportedly closed 138,100 from 30 investors in July 2014 (a later search could not tie Wefunder to Camperoo, so treat as unverified); Village lists 1.6M. Website futureleague.co is a Namecheap parking page. Sigby entry is from an article title only. Education not found.
